historical_references.reference: Iben, or Ibensen, was a Norwegian bishop who lived during the late Middle Ages. He was born around 1260 in Søndre Nordfjord and educated at the University of Oslo. Iben became a priest and served as a canon at St. Olav's Cathedral in Trondheim. In 1314, he was appointed Bishop of Oslo by Pope John XXII. Iben was known for his piety and devotion to the church. He died on February 25, 1330.

Iben Hund (c. 1580–1652) was a Danish nobleman and statesman. He was born in Jutland and studied law in Ribe and Copenhagen. Iben rose to prominence in the Danish court during the reign of King Christian IV. He held various offices, including the position of Chancellor of Denmark, from 1622 until 1628. Iben is best known for his role in the Kalmar Union, a political union of Denmark, Norway, and Sweden, which he helped to establish in 1611. He died in Copenhagen.
